1#main: Things forbidden to a mourner. And it contains 25 seifim. These are things forbidden to a mourner: melacha, bathing, anointing, wearing shoes, use of the bed; forbidden to read Torah; forbidden to greet; forbidden laundry; obligated in covering the head and overturning the bed all seven days; forbidden to put on tefillin on the first day; forbidden pressing clothes, haircut, joy, and sewing a tear all thirty days: {Rama: (and all matters of mourning apply both by day and by night) (in responsum of Rashba siman 400).}
2#main: Melacha — how so? All three first days forbidden in melacha, even a poor person sustained from charity; from then on, if he is poor and has nothing to eat, he does work in private within his house; and a woman may spin on a distaff within her house; but the Sages said, A curse should come upon his neighbors who compelled him to this: {Rama: (As one is permitted to write on chol haMoed, so permitted to write on mourning days, but not another matter) (Kol Bo in the name of R' Meir of Rothenburg and Beit Yosef end of this).}
3#main: Just as he is forbidden in doing melacha, so he is forbidden to buy and sell merchandise and to travel from province to province with merchandise.
4#main: Even a matter of loss — the mourner is forbidden to do, whether he himself, his slaves and maidservants, and his sons and daughters whose handiwork is his.
5#main: Forbidden to have his work done by others: {Rama: (even a non-Jew) (Mordechai beginning chapter Mi SheHafkhah);} unless it is a matter of loss, for a matter of loss a mourner is permitted through others; even something forbidden on chol haMoed due to exertion is permitted, even skilled craft: {Rama: Some say if he cannot do through others and it is a matter of loss, the mourner may do himself (Tur in the name of Ramban and Rosh and so Rabbeinu Yerucham wrote); and after the first three days one may be lenient, even within three if the loss is great.}
6#main: His merchandise in a matter of loss — if he will not sell he loses from the principal, it is sold through others; but if he will not lose from the principal, only that if he sells now he profits more than if he sells later — forbidden; nevertheless if caravans or ships came, or they seek to depart and sell cheap or buy dear, permitted to sell and buy through others, even not for his personal use but to do merchandise for profit.
7#main: To lend to gentiles at interest — for those accustomed to borrow from him, permitted to lend them through others because it is a matter of loss.
8#main: If he used to extract money from people and now cannot find them, and afterward will not find them — permitted to send others to demand from them.
9#main: If he has a case against someone, he does not claim all seven; and if it is a matter of loss, such as he needed to travel to overseas provinces, or his witnesses are still sick — he appoints an agent and judges with him.
10#main: All things permitted on chol haMoed due to need of the festival — all are forbidden for a mourner, even through others.
11#main: A mourner whose field is in others' hands by sharecropping, lease, or contract-work — these work as usual on the mourning days of the field owner; even if their lease term ended earlier and they remained on the field as before.
12#main: If the mourner is a sharecropper on another's field — he may not work himself, but through others is permitted.
13#main: If there is a day-wage worker working the mourner's field, even in another city — he may not work.
14#main: If the mourner has a donkey or ship rented or leased in another's hands — this one may not work on the mourning days of the donkey or ship owner unless he rented before mourning began and the term has not ended; but if the term ended — forbidden.
15#main: If the donkey and ship were in others' hands for half, third, or quarter — some permit and some forbid.
16#main: If the mourner is hired out to another — he may not do melacha on his mourning days: {Rama: (but through others permitted) (so Maharosh).}
17#main: If others' work was in his hands, even detached matter such as weaving, whether with contract-work or without — he may not do: {Rama: And if it is a matter of loss he may do through others (Da'at Emet); permitted to accept work on his mourning days to do later, provided he not weigh or measure as he does at other times (Mordechai Laws of Mourning).}
18#main: If his work was in others' hands as contract-work on detached matter in his house — they may not do; in another's house they may do: {Rama: (provided they accepted the work before mourning began) (Mordechai end of Moed Katan and Rabbeinu Yerucham).}
19#main: If he had building in others' hands as contract-work on a weekday or chol haMoed — they may not do, even outside the city boundary; but if those contractors are gentiles, permitted to build for him on Shabbat and festival that fall on mourning days if outside the city boundary and there is no other city with Jews within the boundary of that house.
20#main: If others accepted to plow and sow his field — some say permitted to plow and sow on mourning days of the field owner; and some forbid.
21#main: Two storekeeper partners, mourning befell one — they close their shop so the partner not work publicly; but he may work in private in his house even in the partnership business; and if the mourner is an important person and the partnership is called by his name, that even if he works in private in his house it is known the mourner has a share — forbidden for both to work, even in his house.
22#main: Honor of the house — rinsing cups and spreading beds is not melacha for a mourner; and likewise a woman may bake and cook on her mourning days: {Rama: (All the mourner needs is permitted; what she does not need is forbidden);} and likewise a woman serving in a house — one mourning is permitted to bake, cook, and do other house needs, whether she serves free or for wages.
23#main: One traveling place to place for trade who heard close tidings — if he can minimize not doing any business in that city it is better; if not, that if he does not buy in that city he will not find — he buys for the road things needed for life.
24#main: For all the dead he may minimize permitted trade business; as a matter of loss he minimizes; he may not minimize for father and mother — he minimizes.
25#main: For all the dead forbidden until thirty days to travel far with merchandise, for there is great publicity and it is like joy when one goes in a large caravan and many rejoice on the way for father and mother until companions protest and say, Go with us.
